newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Jobs at risk without reform - Australian industry.
newsitem.headline: Jobs at risk without reform - Australian industry.

text.p: Australia's largest industry association has warned that up to 100,000 full-time jobs are at risk unless radical changes are made to government policies on attracting investment and creating jobs.
The Metal Trades Industry Association (MTIA) report, prepared by the Economist Intelligence Unit, found it was "make or break" time for Australian industry.

"We are falling further and further behind our near neighbours and global competitors, many of whom do not hesitate to use the full range of incentives, including taxation incentives, to attract and retain job-creating investments," MTIA chief executive Bob Herbert said in a statement.

If local policy settings did not change substantially, Herbert said the report made it clear that many companies, of all sizes, would be attracted to relocate some or all of their manufacturing activities overseas.
"These responses will drive a further shrinking of our industrial base and jeopardise between 85,000 and 100,000 full-time jobs in industry over the next four years," he said.

The MTIA report outlined seven steps it said were needed to get back in the investment and jobs race, including the need to continue delivering good macroeconomic results and introduce fundamental tax reform.

There was also a need for reforms to investment incentives and industrial relations, and also to link the Closer Economic Agreement between Australia and New Zealand to the ASEAN (Association of South East Nations) Free Trade Area.
Finally, the report called for the establishment of a powerful Australian investment agency and to establish strong, central co-ordination of industry policy.
